guest.bio_context: Louis Baxley brings experience from larger enterprise model 3PLs, some of the largest names in the country, and now applies those insights at Fetch Freight, a company built around small and mid-sized shippers. He leads the sales team with a focus on relationship-driven transportation partnerships rather than transactional approaches.

pending_qa.q: What role does technology play in modern transportation partnerships, and why must it be supported by human expertise?
pending_qa.r: Technology is meant to complement rather than replace the relationship side of things. In the current environment driven by data center and AI facility construction, technology adds value through real-time visibility and on-site project manager updates; it also reduces man hours by eliminating redundant customer calls asking for shipment status. However, technology must be backed by people who can act on the information and ensure applicability for end users, whether shipping partners or their customers.

pending_qa.q: How can a mid-sized transportation provider deliver enterprise-level service while maintaining agility?
pending_qa.r: Fetch combines the advantages of larger enterprise models—multiple departments like carrier sales, operations, account management, customer sales, and technology—with small and mid-sized business accessibility; team members are on a first-name basis and bring diverse perspectives from different sides of shipping operations. The company is built for scalability to service large enterprise accounts while remaining nimble enough to customize and tailor processes specifically to various shipping industries and business sectors, which larger providers cannot do as effectively.

pending_qa.q: What criteria should shippers evaluate beyond pricing when selecting a transportation partner?
pending_qa.r: Shippers should emphasize responsiveness, communication level, and speed of communication, ensuring that communication flows freely and constantly whether it is good, bad, or indifferent. Quality indicators also include how quick and accurate the partner is with information; these factors are foundational to evaluating the quality of a partner beyond rates.

pending_qa.q: How does understanding industrial and infrastructure demand shape transportation strategy?
pending_qa.r: The explosion of data centers and AI facilities has brought industrial manufacturing demand that contributes to large-scale industrial projects across the country; these projects are constructed quickly and built seemingly overnight. Transportation providers must work closely with job site and project managers, ensuring on-site contacts have updated information about what is coming and when, requiring tight integration of technology and real-time visibility to support rapid construction timelines.
